findings.text: Upheld as advisory (Q11). The rollback sentence says `share names` lists 'the names the copy will lose', but it lists every current name. It also places the step 'before the `cp`', which comes after the block's `docker compose stop server` (line 77), when no member can reach the server. The step fails visibly and the kept-aside file still holds the names, so this is a documentation inaccuracy and not a broken behaviour.
Upheld as advisory (Q1). The `unknown-name` and `exists` sentences name CLI flags, and the viewer shows the same sentences. Carried from round 2 with the same severity.
Upheld as advisory (Q2, boilerplate). The `names.<state>` flags are cleared in a third place, and backup.ts writes its own `'names.%'` literal. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q2, boilerplate). The bare-404 contract step-down is written three times (lines 227, 318, 378). Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q2). `pushUnderContract` repeats the 409 step-down that inbound's `fetchPage` writes inline. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q8). This re-export duplicates names that callers import from src/sharing/types.ts. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q9). The throw guards a case the key type rules out, and it throws loudly, so it hides nothing. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q5). `currentItemsUnder` only forwards to `nameCountsOf` for its one caller. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q3/Q6). The contract that brought shared names is still a bare `2` in several places, with no named constant. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q6). On a create or join at `all`, the imported count prints twice. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q2). This is partly fixed, but `levelPhrase` and the create and join questions still copy the CLI's text.
Upheld as advisory (Q9). When the given id is already in use, `POST /v1/names` makes a new id and still answers 201, without saying so. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q11). The withdrawal sentence leaves out the held-withdrawal case (D-10). Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q10). The comment narrates the change ('as before') instead of saying why. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q4). AC-48 is observed, and the reason recorded for having no red is the engine's limit. The assertion does pin the rule and would fail on reversion. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q1, partial). AC-44's 'no request' is checked against only one path, so a `/v1/me` read or a POST would go unseen. Carried.
Upheld as advisory. The 'in parallel' and 'unstopped' parts of AC-41 are not distinguished by the test. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q2). 'A remote is never listed' holds because of how the fixture is built. Carried.
Upheld as advisory. The no-SQL check is narrow, and AC-40's order 'after `purged`' has no test. Carried.

Upheld as advisory. Three edge cases from the plan are still unwritten: the 101st bound name, no D-10 hold on a `name` refusal, and `one-server` at the CLI. No behaviour criterion is left without a failing test. Carried.
Upheld as advisory. The runtime capitalisation of the created-name sentence is not pinned by a test. The UI capture covers it, and AC-43's constant sentences stay pinned.

Upheld as advisory. A member who knows a lost name's id can re-create it after a restore without proving they created it. This does not widen what a member can do, because any member can already push under any held name. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (personal-data). After `serve purge name`, the alias and the creator columns stay in `team.db`. ADR 0028 states this limit, and only the operator sees these rows. Carried.
Upheld as advisory. `lowerContract` accepts a value of 0 or below from a hostile server. It fails closed, stopping that server as `contract`; a floor of 1 would only harden the input check. Carried.

Upheld as advisory. The browser console logs the spec-pinned 409 in the created, exists and removed captures (review/ui/console-projects-*.json), and the dock shows the refusal as a sentence. The round-2 ruling lowered this to advisory, and nothing has changed since.

Upheld as advisory. The `exists` switch to 'Join a shared name?' does not say why the create was refused. The spec's wording is met (review/ui/projects-exists@1280-dark.png). Round 2's upheld defect, the undeclared `exists` state, is resolved: the state is declared in the manifest and captured at 360, 768 and 1280.
Upheld as advisory. The slug shows in literal Markdown backticks in the dock sentences and the confirmation questions (review/ui/projects-taken@1280-dark.png). Carried.
Upheld as advisory. 'Set the level again' does not name the path that works. The wording is the spec's (review/ui/projects-created@1280-dark.png). Carried.
Upheld as advisory. In the dark scheme, the disabled 'Shared name' field looks the same as the enabled one (review/ui/projects-held@1280-dark.png). Carried.
Upheld as advisory. At 360px the name lines wrap into crowded lines but still read (review/ui/settings-flagged@360-dark.png). Carried.
Upheld as advisory. Once bound, the spec's read-only field is replaced by a clear 'Shared as' sentence (review/ui/projects-remote-too@1280-dark.png). Carried.

Upheld as advisory. Two variants reuse captured templates with strings no capture shows: the reserved-file-name refusal and the post-confirm 'Not changed' toast (review/ui/projects-refused@1280-dark.png, review/ui/projects-not-changed@1280-dark.png). Carried.

Upheld as advisory (Q2). The rollback step asks members for `share names` 'before the `cp`', which comes after `docker compose stop server` (line 77), so the list cannot be read at that point. The step fails visibly with a connection failure, and the rollback still exists with the newer team.db kept aside. Under the rubric this is a manual rollback with a misplaced step, not a missing or unstated rollback.
Upheld as advisory. The ADR's rollback summary omits the 'names held (server at contract 1)' state, which the runbook states correctly. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q1/Q4). A `name` refusal is retried at every sweep with no backoff. It is visible as `missing` in status, doctor and the dock. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q3). `serve purge name` has no dry run. It retires one named alias, is operator-only and needs `--yes`, so the write is limited to one name. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q1). A Receive-only teammate gets no `missing` signal after a restore older than a name. Carried.

Upheld as advisory. The spec states the client rollback and assigns its sentence to the release notes, which the release item owes. Because the rollback and the dependency are stated, this is not an unstated rollback or dependency. Carried.
Upheld as advisory. `FeedItemShape.nameId` is typed as required, but a contract-1 server never sends it. Nothing reaches the gap today, because names are held at contract 1. Carried.
Upheld as advisory. The names contract is still a bare `2` in five places, on both the client and the server, with no named constant. Carried, partly resolved.
Upheld as advisory. The restore clears the flags with its own `'names.%'` literal, a second spelling of a key format the leaf (`nameFlagKey`) owns.
Upheld as advisory (Q2). No index covers `origin`, so `importedStayCounts` scans the memories table. The result is correct; only the cost is affected. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q2). A `GET /v1/names` page makes per-row reads, each on an index, and ADR 0028 records the choice. Carried.
Upheld as advisory (Q2). No index covers `remote_alias` on `knowledge_received`, so each bound name reads that server's received entries twice. Carried.
